How to tailor your feed
From choosing sources to checking the finished issue.
1. Start with sources and the time window
In News & sources, keep the channels and sites you actually want to read. In Digest settings, try a 24-hour window for a daily issue. The schedule determines when the issue is created.
2. Choose which rules evaluate a source

Assign a profile in the source settings to make Horizon use it for every article from that source. With automatic selection, AI chooses from the allowed profiles. If selection fails, Horizon uses a fallback from the allowed set.
3. Define importance and set a threshold

The scoring prompt tells AI what to consider important. If you want only major releases and security fixes, say so in the prompt. With a threshold of 7, items rated 7 or higher pass this stage. Without a threshold, evaluated items pass regardless of score.
4. Decide what to do with repeat coverage
Topic deduplication can merge articles about the same event within this profile. Turn it off if you want different coverage to stay separate. Basic duplicate checks during collection still apply.
5. Set the size of the issue

After filtering, Horizon takes items in score order, applies group maxima, and then applies the total cap. For example, try 20 items overall and a maximum of 5 from one topic. A quota does not reserve places or guarantee five items.
6. Check an issue and adjust one thing at a time

Save your changes and run a digest. If a topic is missing, check its sources, time window and profile first. If too many low-value stories pass, refine the scoring prompt or raise the threshold. Changes apply to new issues.
